Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] Senator [[Chuck Grassley]] defeated [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] nominee [[Michael Franken]] to win re-election to an eighth term.{{Cite web |title=Chuck Grassley Defeats Mike Franken, Wins Eighth Senate Term |url=https://nz.news.yahoo.com/chuck-grassley-defeats-mike-franken-035134865.html |access-date=November 9, 2022 |website=nz.news.yahoo.com |date=November 9, 2022 |language=en-NZ}} Grassley was first elected in [[1980 United States Senate election in Iowa|1980]] and was most recently re-elected in [[2016 United States Senate election in Iowa|2016]]. Grassley, who turned 89 years old on September 17, 2022, ran for reelection to an eighth term. With U.S. Senator [[Patrick Leahy]] retiring the same year, he became the second-oldest person ever to be re-elected for another term (behind [[Strom Thurmond]] in [[1996 United States Senate election in South Carolina|1996]] at age 93), on January 3, 2023, upon the departure of [[Patrick Leahy]] from the United States Senate [[Chuck Grassley]] became the most senior member in the Senate, and on January 4, 2023, he became the longest-serving Republican senator in history (overtaking [[Orrin Hatch]]), as well as [[List of members of the United States Congress by longevity of service|the most senior member of Congress]] since January 3, 2023. The Republican Party flipped [[Iowa's 3rd congressional district]] in the [[2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Iowa|concurrent House election]], thus marking the first time since 1957 that Iowa had an entirely Republican congressional delegation. Despite his victory, this was Grassley's closest Senate race since he was first elected in [[1980 United States Senate election in Iowa|1980]], as well as his worst performance since that time due to him not cracking 60% of the vote. Franken defeated Grassley in [[Linn County, Iowa|Linn]], [[Story County, Iowa|Story]], and [[Polk County, Iowa|Polk]] counties, all of which Grassley won in every election since [[1986 United States Senate election in Iowa|1986]]. In addition, this election was the first time that Grassley lost [[Black Hawk County, Iowa|Black Hawk]] County. ==Republican primary== [[File:Iowa State Senator Jim Carlin (cropped).jpg|thumb|x170px|State Senator [[Jim Carlin (politician)|Jim Carlin]] challenged Grassley in the primary.]] ===Candidates=== ====Nominee==== *[[Chuck Grassley]], incumbent U.S. senator (1981–present) and [[President pro tempore emeritus of the United States Senate|president pro tempore emeritus]]{{Cite web|date=September 24, 2021|title=Grassley will seek reelection, boosting GOP's majority hopes|url=https://www.politico.com/news/2021/09/24/chuck-grassley-2022-elections-iowa-514090|access-date=September 24, 2021|website=[[Politico]]|language=en}} ====Eliminated in primary==== *[[Jim Carlin (politician)|Jim Carlin]], [[Iowa Senate|state senator]] from the [[Iowa's 3rd Senate district|3rd district]] (2017–2023){{Cite web|last=Hall|first=Jacob|date=February 12, 2021|title=BREAKING: State Sen.
